# llms.txt — @fams/v5-kit export index (hand-authored — see
# packages/skeleton-kit/llms.txt's header for why). Every current barrel
# export symbol name must appear somewhere below as a whole word;
# `pnpm build:llms -- --check` (wired into `pnpm lint`) enforces it.
# format: Symbol(s) :: purpose :: key signature/props :: file

bootstrapTenant :: The one async boot call — turns a tenant's licensed-module list into the skeleton-kit module contract (licensed-only route registration, decision #23), wires the composer blueprint path, applies tenant theming, and sets up privilege gating + query-cache hygiene. Defaults `shellComponent` to `V5AppShell` (below) so every v5-tier app gets the real chrome for free; `BootstrapTenantConfig.shellComponent` overrides it. :: bootstrapTenant(config: BootstrapTenantConfig) → Promise<ResolvedTenant> :: src/bootstrap.tsx
AppsProvider, useApps, AppDefinition, AppsContextValue, AppsProviderProps :: Feeds `V5AppShell` a tenant's outer-rail APPLICATION grouping (a named group of modules, e.g. "Telematics") + branding, without widening skeleton-kit's product-agnostic shell contract (decision #13). `bootstrapTenant` wraps the booted app in this provider; `useApps` (safe outside a provider — defaults to no applications/no logo) is how `V5AppShell` reads it. :: <AppsProvider value={{ applications, logo }}>…</AppsProvider>; useApps() → AppsContextValue :: src/apps.tsx
V5AppShell, V5AppShellProps :: The real v5 application chrome — composes `@fams/ui-kit`'s `AppShell`/`NavRail`(unified expandable rail)/`TopNav` from the generic `FamsModule[]` contract (reusing skeleton-kit's `deriveNavEntries`), matching `SideNav`'s active item to the current TanStack Router location and showing the active module's label as the `TopNav` brand (falling back to `brandLabel` on the index route). This is the `shellComponent` `bootstrapTenant` wires by default. :: V5AppShell({ modules, brandLabel? }: V5AppShellProps) :: src/shell.tsx
resolveTenantModules, ResolveTenantOptions :: Iterates the tenant's LICENSED module codes and reads `implementations[code]` only for a licensed code — an unlicensed implementation present in the map is never referenced, so its lazy `routes` loader is never touched (decision #23, asserted by a spy test). :: resolveTenantModules(licensed: LicensedModule[], options: ResolveTenantOptions) → FamsModule[] :: src/modules.ts
resolveLandingPath, FIRST_MODULE :: Resolves a tenant's optional `landingModule` (a module id, or the literal `FIRST_MODULE` = "first" meaning the first entry of the tenant's ordered modules) to the route path the index route `/` redirects to. Unset → undefined (`/` keeps rendering the V5Home launch pad); an id matching no resolved module → undefined + a loud dev warning, so a bad config lands on Home instead of a dead route. Home's own route and nav entry are untouched either way. :: resolveLandingPath(landingModule: string | undefined, modules: FamsModule[]) → string | undefined :: src/landing.ts
applyTenantTheme :: Applies a tenant's runtime theme (data-tenant + token overrides) on top of skeleton-kit's data-theme bootstrap. :: applyTenantTheme(tenant: string) :: src/theming.ts
PrivilegeProvider, Privileged, usePrivilege, PrivilegeProviderProps, PrivilegedProps, PrivilegeContextValue :: The `v-privilege` rewrite — reactive privilege gating. UI GATING IS UX ONLY (decision #23): these decide what UI to show, never what a user may *do* — real authorization is server-side, per-endpoint, on the untouched v5 API. :: <Privileged requires="…"> …; usePrivilege() → PrivilegeContextValue :: src/privilege.tsx
wipeTenantCache :: Per-tenant TanStack Query cache hygiene — wipes the cache on logout/tenant-switch so no data from one tenant/session leaks into the next. :: wipeTenantCache(queryClient) :: src/cache.ts
ComposerModuleView, makeComposerRouteLoader, ComposerModulePending, ComposerModuleViewProps :: Wires a `FamsModule` route to the v5-composer blueprint path — a route loader that resolves the module's blueprint and renders it via `ComposerModuleView`. :: makeComposerRouteLoader(moduleCode: string) → ModuleRouteLoader :: src/composer-route.tsx
ComposerModulePending, ComposerModulePendingProps, ComposerPendingShape :: The composer route's first paint while a blueprint resolves — a structural skeleton reserving the module surface's real geometry so navigation never lands on a blank page. The geometry MATCHES the module's view kind (`shape`: neutral | list | kanban | split | dashboard, derived from the licensed module's `meta.layout_config.views`); only `split`/`dashboard` get the metric strip, and the default is the neutral single-body frame. :: ComposerModulePending(props: ComposerModulePendingProps) :: src/composer-route.tsx
LicensedModule, LicensedModuleMeta, LicensedModuleMenu, LayoutConfig, ModuleConfigMeta, ModulesSource, PrivilegeUser, UserIdentity, UserSource, BlueprintSource, ModuleImplementation, ModuleImplementationMap, TenantRuntimeConfig, RailStartEntry, ComposerConfig, BootstrapTenantConfig, ResolvedTenant, V5App :: The tenant-boot type vocabulary — a tenant's licensed modules, its injectable data seams (`ModulesSource`/`UserSource`/`BlueprintSource` — real API later, `@fams/demo-kit` today), and the fully-resolved `V5App` `bootstrapTenant` returns. :: BootstrapTenantConfig { modules: ModulesSource, user: UserSource, blueprints: BlueprintSource, … } :: src/types.ts
createRailIndicators, RailIndicatorSource, RailIndicatorController :: Rail-indicator seam — cross-module notification dots for pinned outer-rail entries (e.g. the inbox unread dot): a subscribable `RailIndicatorSource` the shell reads with `useSyncExternalStore`, plus the reference `createRailIndicators()` controller apps push state into. :: createRailIndicators({ inbox: true }).set("inbox", false) :: src/rail-indicators.ts
V5Home, V5CommandPalette, buildLaunchCatalog, V5HomeProps, LaunchCatalogEntry :: The launch-pad Home surface (default index route) and the global ⌘K/Ctrl+K command palette, both derived from the SAME tenant metadata via `buildLaunchCatalog(modules, applications)` — applications × resolved module nav entries, token accent cycle per application; no hardcoded catalog. `V5Home` composes `@fams/v5-templates`' `HomeLaunchPad` (pins persisted per tenant via `usePinnedIds`); `V5CommandPalette` composes ui-kit's `CommandDialog` and is mounted globally by `V5AppShell`. :: buildLaunchCatalog(modules, applications, fallbackLabel?) → { groups, entries } :: src/home.tsx
